podcast.body: This single from the *Sonic Highways* album features a particular passage about 90 seconds into the song that some argue is a "subtle tribute to Ronnie James Dio and his song, Holy Diver." Dave Grohl is known as a metal fan, suggesting he would have been aware of the Dio song. While "not exactly the same," it led to some accusations of a "rip-off," though it's largely explained as homage, and no legal action was taken. "I'm going to argue that this is a subtle tribute to Ronnie James Dio and his song, Holy Diver."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This was the first single released from the "Sonic Highways" album. It was recorded at Electrical Audio in Chicago, a studio owned by Steve Albini, who previously recorded Nirvana's "In Utero." The track features guest guitar contributions from Rick Nielsen of Cheap Trick, a band that was a major favorite of the Foo Fighters members during their youth. "Something from nothing, the first single from the Foo Fighters 2014 album, Sonic Highways."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
